spiritual_reading.full_translation: Within the Divine realm of wisdom, the Divine established the whole order of heaven. I was in a supreme state of that realm, and from it I will disclose to you the realities that are interior and prior. In that interior state, perception is alive because it is borne and actuated by the living proceeding from the Divine. From wisdom’s shining and from the Divine presence there flows an outgo that makes what is within manifest; and within the organized heavens there is the present fullness of greatness, sending forth the acknowledgment of worship in living delight. A sufficient set of operative powers is conjoined into one, so that together they appear as a single spiritual form, and within that form the common atmosphere of life and the inmost vital activity are both living. As that sufficient set is cleansed from every opposition and striving that belongs to the establishing of greatness, it is delivered into concord, and a beautiful unity is formed through the whole complex of faculties, so that the entire spiritual person stands as a likeness of the Divine Human within the realm of wisdom, and life is in each part. Just as every heavenly and spiritual community, every abundance of good, and every ministering function that is called into use proceeds from the Divine, so also every elevation of state, every rising of interior truth, and every perception bearing uses proceeds from that same source and continually flows forth; great is the wonder that everything you perceive lives from that proceeding, and nothing is life from itself. These are ordered realities established in their proper bounds, though the intended sequence breaks where the words are missing. There is also a further degree in which wisdom in a third discrete level and the living common atmosphere of heaven are the dwelling-place of the higher states of greatness, fixed there as forms; and in it are ministering powers in stable function, and the stored gifts and endowments that the Divine bestows within the organized heavens of wisdom. Blessed is the one who comes into knowledge of these things.

paragraph_translations.translation: Within the Divine realm of wisdom, the Divine established the whole order of heaven.
paragraph_translations.notes: The bracketed clause is incomplete; translation assumes “Father” as the Divine source and “Land of Light” as the realm of wisdom/illumination.

paragraph_translations.translation: I was in a supreme state of that realm, and from it I will disclose to you the realities that are interior and prior.
paragraph_translations.notes: Text is fragmentary; “above” is rendered as interior/prior.

paragraph_translations.translation: In that interior state, perception is alive because it is borne and actuated by the living proceeding from the Divine.
paragraph_translations.notes: The surviving words are too broken to fix the subject precisely; “surface” is taken as the outward perceptible form of an interior state.

paragraph_translations.notes: Heavily damaged: the exact relations among clauses are uncertain. “Face,” “rays,” “praise,” “ambrosia,” “five powers,” “image,” “air/breath” are translated by function into presence, worship, delight of good, sufficiency of powers, unified form, and common vital atmosphere.

paragraph_translations.translation: As that sufficient set is cleansed from every opposition and striving that belongs to the establishing of greatness, it is delivered into concord, and a beautiful unity is formed through the whole complex of faculties, so that the entire spiritual person stands as a likeness of the Divine Human within the realm of wisdom, and life is in each part.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Contests” taken as temptations/oppositions; “limbs of their body” as faculties of a whole; “great Man” as the Divine Human (functionally). Some words are lost, so agency (“those five”) is inferred.

paragraph_translations.translation: Just as every heavenly and spiritual community, every abundance of good, and every ministering function that is called into use proceeds from the Divine, so also every elevation of state, every rising of interior truth, and every perception bearing uses proceeds from that same source and continually flows forth; great is the wonder that everything you perceive lives from that proceeding, and nothing is life from itself.
paragraph_translations.notes: The final phrase “neither water nor fire” is too broken to render determinately; the translation keeps the intended doctrinal contrast (nothing lives from itself) without forcing a specific dualism.

paragraph_translations.translation: These are ordered realities, each fixed within its proper bounds.
paragraph_translations.notes: Extremely fragmentary; “measures” rendered as proper bounds/order.

paragraph_translations.translation: There is a further degree in which wisdom in a third discrete level and the living common atmosphere of heaven are the dwelling-place of the higher states of greatness, fixed there as forms; and in it are ministering powers in stable function, and the stored gifts and endowments that the Divine bestows within the organized heavens of wisdom.
paragraph_translations.notes: Broken syntax throughout. “Third degree” rendered as a third discrete level; “aeons” as organized heavenly states; “treasures/gifts” as Divine endowments. Several predicates are missing.

paragraph_translations.translation: Blessed is the one who comes into knowledge of these things.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Moderate coherence in broad outline (a realm of wisdom, proceeding life, conjoined powers forming a unified spiritual person, degrees of heaven, ministering functions, and blessedness of knowing). Coherence weakens sharply in paragraphs 3–4 and 8 due to missing verbs and broken clauses, which forces inferred subjects and connective tissue; paragraph 7 is nearly contentless beyond order and measure. The voice feels mostly consistent as a visionary description of ordered heavenly degrees, with several hard breaks where the surviving words cannot determine the intended sequence.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential opening: establishes a realm (‘Land of Light’) by its function as the place where the Father ‘established all things.’ No administrative inventory or jurisdictional naming intrudes.
findings.evidence: Text: “The Father established all things in] the Land of Light.” The spiritual reading can directly narrate this as a functional cosmological ground (“the whole order of heaven”), and it does not stumble here.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damage, not insertion: first-person visionary transition to disclosure of ‘things…above.’ The narrative continues smoothly; the uncertainty is purely reconstructive (missing words).
findings.evidence: Text: “[I was] in the great land of greatness [manner]s I will reveal to you [the things that are set] above.” Reading notes: “Text is fragmentary… ‘above’ is rendered as interior/prior.” The stumble is about fixing sense, not about a foreign voice.

findings.diagnosis: Damaged line produces forced inference (“surface” as perception). The spiritual reading stumbles because the grammatical subject/predicate chain is broken, not because an administrative layer intrudes.
findings.evidence: Text: “[sur]ace is [the] living [oceeding]om [the Father] upon him.” Reading notes: “too broken to fix the subject precisely.” There’s no jurisdictional language or list structure—just an incomplete correspondential claim about a ‘surface’ and ‘living proceeding.’

findings.diagnosis: Correspondential substrate with heavy damage: a functional account of procession (“from the light and his face goes out”), manifestation (rays/praise/ambrosia), and integration (“five powers…compound together…become an image,” then purification/unity/limbs/body/image of the great Man). The reading stumbles because multiple clauses are missing and relationships among them can’t be securely recovered, but the teaching mode remains functional (what light/face/powers do).
findings.evidence: Text (¶4): “From the] light and [his] face [goes] out… fi[rays] of prais[se]… living [am]bros[i]a… the] five [powers]… compound [together] they become an image… the li[i]ing air [and the breath within it is] also living.” Text (¶5): “those five shall [be purified]… contests… a beautiful [unity is formed] to the limbs of their body… [as an image of the great Man] the land of light.” Reading notes: “Heavily damaged… exact relations uncertain… agency (‘those five’) is inferred.” The stumble is connective/grammar, not narrative incoherence from a different voice.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly coherent correspondential expansion (“as… came from the Father, so also…”), but the tail “neither water nor fire” is a damage-seam that invites doctrinal improvisation. The reader explicitly avoids ‘forcing a specific dualism’—that is exactly what damage does at the end of a sentence, not what an insertion does.
findings.evidence: Text: “Just as all the gods… and the [angels w]ho were summoned came from the Father, so also all [moun]tains… springs and trees… gush forth [from him]… every thing that you [see] neither water nor [fire]”. Reading notes: “The final phrase ‘neither water nor fire’ is too broken to render determinately… keeps intended doctrinal contrast… without forcing a specific dualism.” The bulk is functional procession; the dangling “neither…nor…” is a broken contrast clause.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty: an orphaned resumptive line (“These are… established in their measures”) likely depended on now-lost preceding/following material. It feels ‘contentless’ in the reading because the exemplifying material is missing, not because of overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “These ar[e] which [are established in their measures]”. Reading notes: “nearly contentless beyond order and measure.” This is exactly the profile of a lacuna-adjacent summarizing clause.

findings.diagnosis: Damaged correspondential cosmography (degrees/aeons/air/ministering/treasures). The reading stumbles due to broken syntax and missing predicates, not due to administrative jurisdiction. Despite terms like ‘ministering’ and ‘treasures,’ the passage is not organized as an authority-inventory; it describes a ‘degree’ as a dwelling environment where things are ‘established therein.’
findings.evidence: Text: “The [third]-th [degree of the] great light, the living air… in which the aeons of greatness dwell, being established therein… [ministering]… that [stand] and the [treasures of] the… great Father… given… in the [aeons of light]”. Reading notes: “Broken syntax throughout… Several predicates are missing.” There are no named rulers, no jurisdictions (‘over,’ ‘authority’), no ranked lists—just a spatial/functional description of dwelling and establishment.

findings.diagnosis: Clean closure formula (“Blessed is whoever will know these things”). No disruption; matches visionary-teaching cadence.
findings.evidence: Text: “Blessed is whoever will k[w these things]”. Reading notes: “Clean.”

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative overlay or insertion is diagnosable in this chapter. The spiritual reading’s stumbles are overwhelmingly explained by textual damage (¶3–¶4, ¶7–¶8) and a broken contrast clause at the end of ¶6 (“neither water nor fire”), which forces inferred subjects and connective tissue. Recommendations: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, 9 ‘none’ (with ¶3/¶7 flagged as damaged).
